title: Best App for Expats in Asia to Pay a Cleaner, Tutor or Driver Each Month
summary: Who taught you to pay the cleaner, the tutor or the driver each month in a country whose wallets won't let you sign up?
body_markdown:
Who taught you to pay the cleaner, the tutor or the driver each month in a country whose wallets won't let you sign up? The best app for the job pays them on the local rail they already use, in local currency, and does not require you to open a local bank account. For expats, Moreta Pay does this on national QR networks such as[DuitNow](https://moretapay.com/networks/duitnow) in Malaysia,[KHQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/khqr) in Cambodia,[QR Ph](https://moretapay.com/networks/qr-ph) in the Philippines and[WeChat Pay](https://moretapay.com/networks/wechat-pay) in China. You top up in your home currency, pay their code, and see the exact rate and fee before you confirm. Moreta builds payment access for foreigners on these networks, so the wall between a foreign balance and a local payday is what it works on every day.


**About the Author:**


This guide comes from the team at Moreta Global Inc., a Y Combinator-backed (Summer 2024) Delaware company and FinCEN-registered Money Services Business. Moreta builds Moreta Pay, a wallet that pays local QR networks across Asia and Latin America.


## How do expats usually pay household staff in Asia?


It is the last Friday of the month in Mont Kiara. Your cleaner has just wiped the balcony grille. You are counting 50 MYR notes on the kitchen counter while she waits by the door. The monthly payment to someone you trust is often the clumsiest money you move abroad, and that scene holds the whole problem.


Most expats use one of four methods:


- **ATM cash:**


withdraw, count, hand over. No record unless you write one.


- **Home bank transfer:**


possible if your tutor gives you account details. Cost and timing depend on your bank.


- **International transfer app:**


Wise holds over 40 currencies and sends to over 160 countries, with fees that vary by currency route and payment method. A sensible fit when your driver hands you a bank account number.


- **Local QR payment:**


the way residents pay each other.


In Vietnam, apps like bTaskee and Jup Việc book cleaning helpers by the job


. This guide is about the person you hired directly and pay on the 1st.


## Why can't foreigners just use the local wallets their staff use?


That fourth option is the one locals use, and it is the one most newcomers can't open. Wallets like[MoMo](https://moretapay.com/networks/momo) and Malaysian banking apps are built for residents, so sign-up typically asks for a local phone number, national ID or local bank account. A foreign SIM and a passport rarely get past that screen. The same wall sits behind searches like "vietqr for foreigners."


The way around it comes from how national QR standards work. A national QR standard is like a shared plug socket: every bank and wallet in the country builds to the same shape, so any app that fits the socket can pay any account behind it. DuitNow QR in Malaysia and KHQR in Cambodia work this way. You do not need your cleaner's bank. You need something that fits the socket.


## How do you pay a cleaner, tutor or driver through a local QR network?


Once a wallet fits that socket, payday is four steps. Moreta Pay needs no local bank account and no local SIM:


1. **Add money in your own currency.**


Use US ACH, SEPA (EUR), UK Faster Payments (GBP), Canadian Interac e-Transfer (CAD), Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Apple Pay or Google Pay. USDC or USDT on Solana also works, but stablecoin top-ups can't be spent in Cambodia or China.


2. **Scan their QR code,**


or import the screenshot they send you on WhatsApp.


3. **Check the review screen:**


amount, merchant name, FX rate and fee.


4. **Slide to confirm.**


They receive local currency, and you get a receipt.


One honest caveat: Moreta Pay is built around merchant QR codes. A tutor who invoices through a small business usually has one. If your helper only has a personal account, the Send feature pays a bank account, a local wallet or QR rail, or another Moreta user, with availability depending on country and app version. Make your first payment a small test before payday.


## Which payment method costs the least over a year?


Cost matters more here than for a one-off coffee, because a salary is twelve transactions a year and small percentage gaps compound. Moreta Pay charges a single 1.5% fee per payment, shown before you confirm, with no monthly plan. Its rate calculator estimates about 4.0% for a home bank card and higher costs for ATM cash, based on published prices that vary by bank and location.

Two habits cut costs further:


- **Batch your top-up.**


A USD bank top-up costs 1 USD and is free above 250 USD. SEPA is free above 225 EUR, Faster Payments above 200 GBP. Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay top-ups cost 2.5%. USD bank top-ups take 1-3 business days, so start a few days early.


- **Decline dynamic currency conversion.**


When an ATM or card terminal offers to charge you in your home currency, refuse. Always choose local currency.


## Which Asian countries does this work in, and what are the limits?


The same four steps apply across Moreta's Asian markets. Each country sets a single-payment maximum and a weekly limit, shown in the app before you pay.

The weekly limit is the one to watch. If your cleaner and driver are both paid on the 1st, both salaries count against the same week. In China, payments work only while you are physically in the country, and Moreta pays WeChat Pay codes, not Alipay's.


## When do you still need cash for household staff?


A QR wallet covers the salary, but it does not cover every payment to the people in your home. Festival gifts are still a cash custom:


- **Malaysia:**


duit raya in green packets at Hari Raya. Keep a few crisp 10 MYR notes.


- **China:**


a red hongbao for your ayi before Chinese New Year. Fresh 100 CNY notes are part of the gesture.


- **Vietnam:**


lì xì envelopes at Tết, with new 50,000 or 100,000 VND notes.


Keep that reserve modest and specific. The monthly salary does not need to be in it.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can I pay my cleaner in Asia without a local bank account?


Yes. Moreta Pay requires no local bank account and no local SIM. You top up from home and pay local QR codes.


### Is Moreta a bank?


No. Moreta Global Inc. is a FinCEN-registered Money Services Business. Customer funds are held with licensed partner banks.


### Does my driver need the Moreta app?


No. They receive local currency through their own bank or wallet. If both of you use Moreta, transfers between verified accounts are free, but they can't be refunded.


### Can I fund staff payments with stablecoins in Cambodia or China?


No. Money added with USDC or USDT can't be spent in those two markets. Use a bank or card top-up there.


### What record do I get after paying?


Each receipt shows date, time, amount, merchant name, merchant ID and payment number. That helps if anyone ever asks whether March was paid.


### Should I use Wise instead?


If your tutor gives you a bank account number, Wise is a reasonable choice. Moreta Pay fits staff who are paid by scanning a local QR code.


## What should you set up before the first payday?


Everything above comes down to three tasks you can finish this week:


1. **Verify your account.**


Moreta checks your identity with a selfie and your passport.


2. **Collect each person's QR code.**


Ask for a screenshot and save it, then send a small test payment.


3. **Schedule your top-up.**


Use a bank transfer above the free threshold, timed a few days before the 1st.
